seo.og_title: Taroudant Ramparts: Walk the 7.5 km Walls
seo.og_description: Circle the ochre walls of Taroudant on foot or by calèche — one of the best-preserved fortified circuits in southern Morocco.

name: The Ramparts
hero_subtitle: 7.5 km of intact 16th-century ochre walls around Taroudant, the Little Marrakech of the Souss.

overview.title: A continuous ring of ochre walls
overview.p1: Taroudant’s ramparts form one of the most complete adobe fortification circuits in Morocco. Built mainly in the 16th century under the Saadians, they stretch about 7.5 km, with roughly 130 towers and several monumental gates including Bab el-Kasbah and Bab Targhount.
overview.p2: Walking or riding a calèche along a stretch of the walls is the classic way to feel the scale of the Little Marrakech. Late afternoon light turns the ochre adobe golden.
overview.p3: There is no single ticketed ramparts museum. Follow the path along the walls, stop at gates, and climb only where allowed and safe.

q1.question: Are the Taroudant ramparts free?
q1.answer: Yes. Walking is free. You only pay for a calèche or a paid tour.

q2.question: How long for a full circuit?
q2.answer: On foot, 7.5 km is a long walk (2–3 hours+). Most visitors do a section or a 45–90 min calèche ride.

q3.question: Can you climb the walls?
q3.answer: Only where access is clear and safe. Do not climb damaged sections.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: Sunrise and late afternoon for cooler air and golden light on the ochre adobe.

q5.question: How do I hire a calèche?
q5.answer: Near main gates and squares. Agree price and route before you start.
